# Input format

`dpa-review` reviews a structured JSON description of one Data Processing Agreement, not the contract text. This page lists every key the input may contain. The same contract is published as JSON Schema in [`schema/dpa.schema.json`](../schema/dpa.schema.json) (also printed by `dpa-review --schema`), and both are generated from [`src/dpa_review/contract.py`](../src/dpa_review/contract.py).

## How input is checked

Every input is checked against the contract before any rule runs. Input that breaks it exits `3` and no review state is decided, because a key the rules do not see would otherwise read as "not recorded": a misspelt `"transfer"` section once made a DPA with a US transfer come out `CLEARED_FOR_REVIEW` with exit `0`. Each problem is reported with its line, for example:

```text
error: dpa.json breaks the input contract, so no review state was decided (2 problems):
  line 43: unknown key 'transfer'; did you mean 'transfers'?
  line 1: missing required key 'transfers': record "transfers": {"destinations": []} if the processor makes no direct transfer.
```

- An unknown key, at any level, is refused, with the closest known key as a suggestion.
- A required section or key that is missing or `null` is refused. Record an absence explicitly (`[]`, `false`, `"none"`) instead of leaving the key out.
- A value of the wrong JSON type is refused: the string `"false"` is not a boolean.
- A description (`processing.subject_matter`, `processing.duration`, `processing.nature_and_purpose`) that reads as yes or no, such as `"false"`, is refused: record yes/no as a JSON boolean.
- Country codes are upper-case ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes. `UK`, `EL` and `EU` are refused with the code to use instead (`GB`, `GR`, a member state).
- Every key of `transfers.mechanisms`, and of the other per-country objects under `transfers`, must be a country that `transfers.destinations` lists.
- Sub-processor names must contain a letter or digit and must differ, ignoring case, spaces and punctuation, because rule ids are derived from them.
- Every `evidence` key must name a fact the input records.

A flag that is `false`, `null` or omitted reads as "the DPA does not contain this", so a clause you could not find fails closed.

## The smallest valid input

```json
{
  "processing": {},
  "art28_clauses": {},
  "breach_notification": {},
  "subprocessors": [],
  "transfers": {
    "destinations": []
  }
}
```

It is valid, and `BLOCKED`: it records no Art. 28 clause. [`data/sample_dpa.json`](../data/sample_dpa.json) is a complete example, and [`tests/fixtures/`](../tests/fixtures/) holds 12 more.

## Keys

- `$schema` (string): The URL or path of schema/dpa.schema.json, so an editor can check and complete the file as you type. No rule reads it.
- `agreement` (string): Name of the agreement, used as the packet title. No rule reads it.
- `controller` (string): Name of the controller. Labels the transfer evidence graph; no rule reads it.
- `processor` (string): Name of the processor. Labels the transfer evidence graph; no rule reads it.
- `roles_defined` (boolean, or null): Whether the DPA defines the controller and processor roles. Recorded only: no rule reads it.

### `processing`

Required, an object. The processing details GDPR Art. 28(3) requires the DPA to set out. Read by the processing.* rules.

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `processing.subject_matter` | string or boolean, or null | no | The subject matter of the processing is stated: true, or a short description. Rule processing.subject_matter. |
| `processing.duration` | string or boolean, or null | no | The duration of the processing is stated: true, or a short description. Rule processing.duration. |
| `processing.nature_and_purpose` | string or boolean, or null | no | The nature and purpose of the processing are stated: true, or a short description. Rule processing.nature_and_purpose. |
| `processing.data_types` | list of strings, or null | no | The types of personal data processed. Rule processing.data_types: an empty or omitted list is MISSING. |
| `processing.data_subjects` | list of strings, or null | no | The categories of data subjects. Rule processing.data_subjects: an empty or omitted list is MISSING. |
| `processing.includes_non_hr_data` | boolean, or null | no | Whether non-HR personal data is transferred; null or omitted when the DPA does not say. Read for a dpf transfer: the importer's certification must cover the data transferred. |
| `processing.includes_hr_data` | boolean, or null | no | Whether HR data from the employment context is transferred; null or omitted when the DPA does not say. Read for a dpf transfer: the importer's certification must cover the data transferred. |

### `art28_clauses`

Required, an object. The processor clauses GDPR Art. 28(2)-(4) require. Each flag is true when the DPA contains the clause; false, null or omitted when it was not found.

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `art28_clauses.process_on_documented_instructions` | boolean, or null | no | Art. 28(3)(a): the processor processes only on documented instructions. Rule art28.process_on_documented_instructions. |
| `art28_clauses.confidentiality_commitment` | boolean, or null | no | Art. 28(3)(b): persons authorised to process are bound to confidentiality. Rule art28.confidentiality_commitment. |
| `art28_clauses.security_measures_art32` | boolean, or null | no | Art. 28(3)(c): the processor takes the security measures of Art. 32. Rule art28.security_measures_art32. |
| `art28_clauses.subprocessor_authorization` | one of `specific`, `general`, `none`, or null | no | Art. 28(2): "specific" (prior specific written authorisation), "general" (general written authorisation) or "none". Rule subprocessor.authorization: "none", null or omitted is MISSING. |
| `art28_clauses.subprocessor_flowdown` | boolean, or null | no | Art. 28(4): the same data-protection obligations are imposed on every sub-processor. Rule subprocessor.flowdown. |
| `art28_clauses.assist_data_subject_requests` | boolean, or null | no | Art. 28(3)(e): the processor assists with data-subject requests. Rule art28.assist_data_subject_requests. |
| `art28_clauses.assist_security_breach` | boolean, or null | no | Art. 28(3)(f): the processor assists with security, breach and DPIA obligations (Art. 32-36). Rule art28.assist_security_breach. |
| `art28_clauses.delete_or_return_on_termination` | boolean, or null | no | Art. 28(3)(g): the processor deletes or returns the data at the end of the services. Rule art28.delete_or_return_on_termination. |
| `art28_clauses.audit_and_inspection_rights` | boolean, or null | no | Art. 28(3)(h): the processor allows and contributes to audits and inspections. Rule art28.audit_and_inspection_rights. |

### `breach_notification`

Required, an object. Breach-notification terms (GDPR Art. 33(2)). Read by rule breach.processor_notifies.

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `breach_notification.processor_notifies_controller` | boolean, or null | no | The processor notifies the controller of a personal-data breach. Rule breach.processor_notifies. |
| `breach_notification.timing` | string, or null | no | The notice period as the DPA words it, e.g. "without undue delay". The rule passes only wording that contains "undue delay" or "without delay"; other wording goes to review. |
| `breach_notification.controller_notifies_authority_art33` | boolean, or null | no | The controller's own notice to the supervisory authority is addressed. Recorded only: no rule reads it. |

### `subprocessors`

Required, a list of objects. Every sub-processor the DPA names or authorises. Each one outside the EEA is checked as a transfer (rule transfer.subprocessor.&lt;name&gt;). Record [] when there are none.

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `subprocessors[].name` | non-empty string | yes | The sub-processor's name. Names must contain a letter or digit and must differ, ignoring case, spaces and punctuation, because rule ids are derived from them. |
| `subprocessors[].country` | country code | yes | Upper-case ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the country where it processes the data, e.g. "US" (the United Kingdom is "GB", Greece is "GR"). |
| `subprocessors[].purpose` | string | no | What the sub-processor does. Labels the graph; no rule reads it. |
| `subprocessors[].transfer_mechanism` | one of `none`, `adequacy`, `sccs`, `bcr`, `dpf`, `derogation_art49`, or null | no | The Chapter V basis for a sub-processor outside the EEA. Null or omitted reads as none. |
| `subprocessors[].dpf_certified` | boolean, or null | no | For a dpf mechanism: the sub-processor is actively certified on the Data Privacy Framework List. |
| `subprocessors[].dpf_covers_non_hr_data` | boolean, or null | no | For a dpf mechanism: the sub-processor's DPF certification covers non-HR data. |
| `subprocessors[].dpf_covers_hr_data` | boolean, or null | no | For a dpf mechanism: the sub-processor's DPF certification covers HR data. |
| `subprocessors[].occasional_and_not_repetitive` | boolean, or null | no | For a derogation_art49 mechanism: the transfer is occasional and not repetitive. Otherwise the derogation is treated like a missing basis. |

### `transfers`

Required, an object. Transfers of personal data that the processor makes directly to other countries.

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `transfers.destinations` | list of country codes | yes | Upper-case ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes of every country the processor transfers personal data to directly; each is checked (rule transfer.&lt;country&gt;). Record [] when there are none. |
| `transfers.mechanisms` | object keyed by country code → one of `none`, `adequacy`, `sccs`, `bcr`, `dpf`, `derogation_art49`, or null, or null | no | The Chapter V basis per destination, keyed by a country that destinations lists. A destination without an entry reads as none. |
| `transfers.dpf_certified` | object keyed by country code → boolean, or null, or null | no | For a dpf mechanism, per destination: the importer is actively certified on the Data Privacy Framework List. |
| `transfers.dpf_covers_non_hr_data` | object keyed by country code → boolean, or null, or null | no | For a dpf mechanism, per destination: the importer's DPF certification covers non-HR data. |
| `transfers.dpf_covers_hr_data` | object keyed by country code → boolean, or null, or null | no | For a dpf mechanism, per destination: the importer's DPF certification covers HR data. |
| `transfers.occasional_and_not_repetitive` | object keyed by country code → boolean, or null, or null | no | For a derogation_art49 mechanism, per destination: the transfer is occasional and not repetitive. Otherwise the derogation is treated like a missing basis. |
| `transfers.transfer_impact_assessment` | boolean, or null | no | A transfer impact assessment is recorded. Read only when SCCs or BCR are relied on for a destination or sub-processor outside the EEA (rule transfer.impact_assessment). |

### `ccpa`

Optional, an object. California CCPA/CPRA terms, a secondary lens. Omitted reads as not recorded, which goes to review.

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ccpa.service_provider_terms` | boolean, or null | no | Service-provider terms restricting the sale and retention of personal information are present. Rule ccpa.service_provider_terms. |

### `evidence`

Optional. Where each recorded fact comes from in the DPA, keyed by the fact's path, e.g. {"art28_clauses.subprocessor_flowdown": {"clause": "§ 7.2", "quote": "..."}}. The packet prints it next to the findings that read the fact. A key must name a fact this input records.

Each value has a `clause` (where the fact is in the DPA, such as `"§ 7.2"` or `"Annex 3"`), a `quote` (the DPA's own words, verbatim), or both. A key may name a single fact (`"art28_clauses.subprocessor_flowdown"`), a list item (`"subprocessors[1]"`, which also covers that sub-processor's country and mechanism) or a whole section. The Markdown packet then gains a "Source in the DPA" column, and each finding in the JSON packet an `evidence` list.

```json
{
  "evidence": {
    "art28_clauses.subprocessor_flowdown": {
      "clause": "§ 7.2",
      "quote": "The Processor shall impose the same data protection obligations as set out in this Agreement on every Sub-processor."
    },
    "subprocessors[0]": {
      "clause": "Annex 3"
    }
  }
}
```
